title.english: Ruqayya al-Hashimiyya,[2] daughter of the Master of Mankind—Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib,[1] may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

segments.arabic:
١١١٨٧- رقيّة بنت سيد البشر ﷺ:
محمد بن عبد اللَّه بن عبد المطلب «١» الهاشمية «٢»، هي زوج عثمان بن عفان، وأم ابنه عبد اللَّه.
قال أبو عمر: لا أعرف خلافا أنّ زينب أكبر بنات النبي ﷺ. واختلف في رقية وفاطمة وأم كلثوم، والأكثر أنهنّ على هذا الترتيب. ونقل أبو عمر عن الجرجاني أنه صح أن رقية أصغرهن، وقيل: كانت فاطمة أصغرهن، وكانت رقية أولا عند عتبة بن أبي لهب، فلما بعث النبي ﷺ أمر أبو لهب ابنه بطلاقها، فتزوجها عثمان.
وقال ابن هشام: تزوج عثمان رقية، وهاجر بها إلى الحبشة، فولدت له عبد اللَّه هناك:
فكان يكنى به.
وقال أبو عمر: قال قتادة: لم تلد له، قال: وهو غلط لم يقله غيره، ولعله أراد أختها أم كلثوم، فإنّ عثمان تزوجها بعد رقية، فماتت أيضا عنده، ولم تلد له، قاله ابن شهاب والجمهور. وسيأتي لتزويج رقية ذكر في ترجمة سعدى أم عثمان حماتها.
وقال ابن سعد: بايعت رسول اللَّه ﷺ هي وأخواتها، وتزوجها عتبة بن أبي لهب قبل النبوة، فلما بعث قال أبو لهب: رأسي من رأسك حرام إن لم تطلق ابنته، ففارقها ولم يكن دخل بها، فتزوجها عثمان، فأسقطت منه سقطا، ثم ولدت له بعد ذلك ولدا فسماه عبد اللَّه، وبه كان يكنى، ونقره ديك فمات فلم تلد له بعد ذلك.
وأخرج ابن سعد من طريق عليّ بن زيد، عن يوسف بن مهران، عن ابن عباس، قال: لما ماتت رقية قال النبي ﷺ: «ألحقي بسلفنا عثمان بن مظعون» . فبكت النساء على رقية، فجاء عمر بن الخطاب فجعل يضربهن، فقال النبي ﷺ: «مهما يكون من العين ومن القلب فمن اللَّه والرّحمة، ومهما يكن من اليد واللّسان فمن الشّيطان» «٣» . فقعدت فاطمة على شفير القبر تبكي، فجعل يمسح عن عينها بطرف ثوبه.
قال الواقديّ: هذا وهم، ولعلها غيرها من بناته، لأن الثبت أن رقية ماتت ببدر، أو يحمل على أنه أتى قبرها بعد أن جاء من بدر.
وأخرج ابن مندة بسند واه عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر،
(١) في أ: عبد المطلب بن هاشم الهاشمية.
(٢) أسد الغابة: ت ٦٩٢٩، الاستيعاب: ت ٣٣٨٩.
(٣) أخرجه أحمد في المسند ١/ ٣٣٥ عن ابن عباس.
segments.english:
11187—Ruqayya al-Hashimiyya,[2] daughter of the Master of Mankind—Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib,[1] may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

She was the wife of Uthman ibn Affan and the mother of his son Abd Allah.

Abu Umar said: “I know of no disagreement that Zaynab was the eldest of the Prophet's daughters, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. There is disagreement concerning Ruqayya, Fatima, and Umm Kulthum, though most authorities place them in this order.” Abu Umar related from al-Jurjani that it was established that Ruqayya was the youngest of them. It was also said that Fatima was the youngest. Ruqayya was initially married to Utba ibn Abi Lahab. When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was commissioned, Abu Lahab ordered his son to divorce her, and Uthman then married her.

Ibn Hisham said: “Uthman married Ruqayya and emigrated with her to Abyssinia. There she bore him Abd Allah, after whom he took his kunyah.”

Abu Umar said: “Qatada said that she bore him no children. This is an error which no one else stated. Perhaps he meant her sister Umm Kulthum, whom Uthman married after Ruqayya. She too died while married to him and bore him no children, as Ibn Shihab and the majority stated.” An account of Ruqayya's marriage will appear in the biography of Sa'da, Uthman's mother and Ruqayya's mother-in-law.

Ibn Sa'd said: “She and her sisters pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Utba ibn Abi Lahab married her before the prophethood. When the Prophet was sent forth, Abu Lahab said, ‘My head is forbidden to your head unless you divorce his daughter.’ He therefore separated from her without having consummated the marriage. Uthman then married her. She miscarried a fetus by him, and afterward bore him a son whom he named Abd Allah, after whom he took his kunyah. A rooster pecked the boy, and he died. She bore Uthman no children after that.”

Ibn Sa'd transmitted, through Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Ruqayya died, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Join our predecessor Uthman ibn Maz'un.” The women wept over Ruqayya, and Umar ibn al-Khattab came and began striking them. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whatever proceeds from the eye and the heart is from Allah and from mercy, while whatever proceeds from the hand and the tongue is from Satan.”[3] Fatima sat at the edge of the grave weeping, and he began wiping the tears from her eyes with the edge of his garment.

Al-Waqidi said: “This is an error. Perhaps it concerned another of his daughters, because it is firmly established that Ruqayya died at the time of Badr; alternatively, it may be understood to mean that he came to her grave after returning from Badr.”

Ibn Manda transmitted, with a weak chain of transmission, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Asma bint Abi Bakr,

[1] In manuscript A: “Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim, the Hashimiyya.”

[2] Usd al-Ghaba, entry 6929; al-Isti'ab, entry 3389.

[3] Transmitted in Musnad Ahmad, 1/335, from Ibn Abbas.

segments.arabic:
قالت: كنت أحمل الطعام إلى أبي وهو مع رسول اللَّه ﷺ بالغار، فاستأذنه عثمان في الهجرة، فأذن له في الهجرة إلى الحبشة، فحملت الطعام، فقال لي: «ما فعل عثمان ورقيّة»؟ قلت. قد سارا. فالتفت إلى أبي بكر، فقال: «والّذي نفسي بيده، إنّه أوّل من هاجر بعد إبراهيم ولوط» .
قلت: وفي هذا السياق من النكارة أن هجرة عثمان إلى الحبشة كانت حين هجرة النبي ﷺ، وهذا باطل، إلا إن كان المراد بالغار غير الّذي كانا فيه لما هاجرا إلى المدينة، والّذي عليه أهل السير أنّ عثمان رجع مكة من الحبشة مع إلى من رجع، ثم هاجر بأهله إلى المدينة، ومرضت بالمدينة لما خرج النبي ﷺ إلى بدر، فتخلف عليها عثمان عن بدر، فماتت يوم وصول زيد بن حارثة مبشرا بوقعة بدر. وقيل: وصل لما دفنت.
وروى حماد بن سلمة، عن ثابت، عن أنس، قال: لما ماتت رقية قال رسول اللَّه ﷺ: «لا يدخل القبر رجل قارف» «١» . فلم يدخل عثمان.
قال أبو عمر: هذا خطأ من حماد، إنما كان ذلك في أم كلثوم.
وقد روى ابن المبارك، عن يونس، عن الزهري، قال: تخلف عثمان عن بدر على امرأته رقية، وكانت قد أصابها الحصبة، فماتت، وجاء زيد بشيرا بوقعة بدر، قال: وعثمان على قبر رقية.
ومن طريق قتادة عن النضر بن أنس، عن أبيه: خرج عثمان برقية إلى الحبشة مهاجرا، فاحتبس خبرهما، فأتت النبي ﷺ امرأة فأخبرته أنها رأتهما. فقال النبي ﷺ: «قبّحهما اللَّه، إنّ عثمان أوّل من هاجر بأهله» - يعني من هذه الأمة.
وذكر السّراج في تاريخه من طريق هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، قال: تخلف عثمان، وأسامة بن زيد، عن بدر، فبينا هم يدفنون رقية سمع عثمان تكبيرا، فقال: يا أسامة، ما هذا؟ فنظروا، فإذا زيد بن حارثة على ناقة رسول اللَّه ﷺ الجدعاء بشيرا بقتل المشركين يوم بدر.
segments.english:
She said: “I used to carry food to my father while he was with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the cave. Uthman asked his permission to emigrate, and he gave him permission to emigrate to Abyssinia. I carried the food, and he said to me, ‘What has become of Uthman and Ruqayya?’ I replied, ‘They have already departed.’ He turned to Abu Bakr and said, ‘By Him in whose hand is my soul, he is the first to emigrate after Abraham and Lot.’”

I say: One objectionable feature of this narrative is that it places Uthman's emigration to Abyssinia at the time of the emigration of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. This is false, unless the cave intended is some cave other than the one in which the two of them stayed when they emigrated to Medina. The position maintained by the authorities on the prophetic biography is that Uthman returned to Mecca from Abyssinia with [those] who returned, and then emigrated with his family to Medina. Ruqayya fell ill in Medina when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set out for Badr, so Uthman stayed behind from Badr to care for her. She died on the day Zayd ibn Haritha arrived bearing the good news of the Battle of Badr. It is also said that he arrived when she had been buried.

Hammad ibn Salama related from Thabit, from Anas, who said: When Ruqayya died, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “No man who has qarafa is to enter the grave.”¹ Uthman therefore did not enter it.

Abu Umar said: This is an error on Hammad's part; that occurred only in the case of Umm Kulthum.

Ibn al-Mubarak related from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, who said: Uthman stayed behind from Badr to care for his wife Ruqayya, who had contracted measles. She died, and Zayd came bearing the good news of the Battle of Badr. He said: Uthman was at Ruqayya's grave.

And through Qatada, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from his father: Uthman set out with Ruqayya as an emigrant to Abyssinia, and news of them was delayed. A woman came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and informed him that she had seen them both. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “May Allah disgrace them both! Uthman is the first man to emigrate with his family”—meaning, from this community.

al-Siraj mentioned in his History, through Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, who said: Uthman and Usama ibn Zayd stayed behind from Badr. While they were burying Ruqayya, Uthman heard a proclamation of Allah's greatness and said, “Usama, what is this?” They looked, and there was Zayd ibn Haritha upon al-Jad'a, the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bearing the good news that the polytheists had been slain on the day of Badr.

names.arabic: محمد بن عبد اللَّه بن عبد المطلب
names.english: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib

unresolved.explanation: The sequence is syntactically corrupt. The provisional English “with [those] who returned” treats إلى as intrusive, but neither the Urdu witness nor the supplied collateral passages establish the correct reading. Another Arabic witness of al-Isabah is required.
